California Real‑Estate CEO Sentenced to 18 Months for Concealing $2.2 Million Investor Losses

02 Nov 2026, 08:31 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: timesofindia.indiatimes.com

3 min read

Key takeaways--- The article is based on publicly released government statements and court documents. No original reporting was conducted.

  1. Court Verdict
  2. How the Scheme Operated

Court Verdict

A federal judge in California has sentenced former SiliconSage Builders president and CEO Sanjeev Acharya to 18 months in prison for wire fraud and money‑laundering. The ruling, issued by U.S. District Judge Charles R. Breyer, also includes two years of supervised release and a restitution order of $2,253,219.84 to more than 20 investors.

How the Scheme Operated

  • Company profile: SiliconSage Builders and affiliated firms were marketed as a vertically integrated developer of large residential and mixed‑use projects in the San Francisco Bay Area.
  • Financial trouble: By early 2020 the business was heavily indebted and suffering cash‑flow shortages, a condition the company attributed to the COVID‑19 pandemic.
  • Misleading conduct: From March 2020 through October 26 2020, Acharya solicited new investments while *knowingly* hiding the firm’s debt and liquidity problems. He presented the projects as financially sound and urged investors to fund construction.
  • Investor impact: More than 20 individuals placed money with the expectation that it would support viable developments. The undisclosed financial distress meant the new capital was used to keep the existing operation afloat, not to expand projects. Collectively, the investors lost over $2.2 million.

Legal Proceedings

  • Charges: Wire fraud (using electronic communications to execute a scheme) and a money‑laundering‑related offense involving the handling of fraud‑derived funds.
  • Plea: Acharya pleaded guilty on Jan 6 2026, avoiding a trial.
  • Investigation: Conducted by the IRS Criminal Investigation (IRS‑CI) team, which traced the flow of funds and identified the concealment of material financial information.
  • Prosecution: Led by Assistant U.S. Attorney Christiaan Highsmith, with support from Janice Pagsanjan, Mimi Lam, and Kevin Costello.

Confirmed vs. Reported Information

  • Confirmed: The 18‑month prison term, restitution amount, and the fact that the scheme ran from March to October 2020.
  • Reported by the U.S. Attorney’s Office: More than 20 investors were deceived and suffered losses exceeding $2.2 million.
  • Unknown: Whether any civil actions are pending against the company’s assets or if Acharya will appeal the sentence.

Practical Implications for Investors

  • Due diligence: Verify a developer’s financial statements, debt levels, and any pending litigation before committing funds.
  • Regulatory checks: Confirm that the offering is registered with the SEC or qualified for an exemption; unregistered offerings carry higher risk.
  • Red flags: Promises of high returns, pressure to invest quickly, and lack of transparent financial disclosures should trigger caution.

How to Verify the Announcement

  • Court records: The case docket (U.S. District Court, Northern District of California) is publicly accessible via PACER.
  • Official press release: The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of California posted a release on Oct 28 2026, which can be found on its website.
  • IRS‑CI statement: The agency’s public statements and the accompanying press release provide additional confirmation of the investigation’s scope.

--- *The article is based on publicly released government statements and court documents. No original reporting was conducted.*
